dominant_breach: institutional single-family rental ownership may be small in aggregate yet locally material, and corporate landlord systems can convert access to family-sized rental homes into fee, repair, renewal, and security-deposit extraction
fastest_washout: moving costs, school catchment attachment, opaque fee stacks, maintenance delays, lease-renewal pressure, and security-deposit disputes wash out renter savings and exit power

rental_market_power_gate.note: Aggregate institutional ownership can be low while metro/neighborhood concentration, fee practices, and repair systems still create ordinary-claimant extraction.

institutional_single_family_rental_conce.note: GAO evidence requires local-market scoring: low national share cannot certify benignity where owner concentration, school catchments, and family-home scarcity create localized extraction power.

corporate_landlord_fee_stack.note: The Invitation Homes enforcement/refund record converts fee stacks, repair failures, and security-deposit disputes into active household-market extraction evidence.

security_deposit_repair_remedy_access.note: Active certification requires tenant-level restoration evidence: inspection quality, repair response, deposit return, refund delivery, and repeat-violation prevention.

build_to_rent_supply_offset.note: Some institutional/built-for-rent supply may add rental homes; the cube needs local supply-offset evidence before treating ownership as uniformly harmful.

local_investor_concentration_visibility.note: Portfolio concentration must be visible by parcel, owner, beneficial owner, market, and school catchment, not only national totals.

renter_cost_burden.note: Renter cost-burden context makes small recurring fees and rent increases material to household wealth formation.

housing_market_power_remedy_access.note: Refunds and settlement conditions are evidence of remedy, but the cube needs recurring compliance and claim-restoration data.

proof_debt: metro/neighborhood concentration by owner and beneficial owner
all-in lease cost, fee, repair, and deposit incidence by household group
supply-offset evidence for build-to-rent versus acquisition of owner-occupant stock
tenant complaint, refund, and restoration outcomes

gate_05_washout_reconcentration.why: Fee, repair, and deposit practices can reconcentrate household gains into landlord revenue, especially where moving is costly.

gate_06_wealth_to_rule_capture.why: Institutional ownership needs local-concentration scoring before it can be treated as benign or harmful in aggregate.

gate_10_measurement_uncertainty_owner_vi.why: National shares conceal local portfolio concentration and beneficial ownership structures.

gate_11_enforceability_remedies_capture_.why: Corporate-landlord claims require tenant complaint, refund, and restoration data, not merely enforcement announcements.

gate_15_place_public_finance_service_wea.why: School, commute, and neighborhood attachment can make single-family rental exit power weaker than ordinary apartment mobility.

gate_16_household_market_extraction_cost.why: Hidden fees, repair burdens, and deposit losses are recurring household-market extraction channels.
